transcript.text: I can help with that. 'Stopped working' usually points to one of three things: no power getting in (plug, cord, or battery), a safety cut-out triggered by a blockage or overheating, or an internal failure. To narrow this down quickly, please tell me if it is a corded vacuum or a battery/cordless model?
its corded, the red Henry one with the face. no power at all when I switch it on

The issue is probably in the power supply path: the wall socket, the plug fuse, the mains cable, or the on/off switch. The most common cause is a blown 13A fuse in the plug or a faulty socket. Please try plugging the vacuum into a different, known-working wall socket first. If it still does nothing, please check the plug fuse (if accessible) or inspect the cable for any visible cuts or damage near the plug and handle.

I tried the lamp in the same socket and it works. Hoover still nothing in another socket too. There's old black tape on the cable near the plug, my son did it ages ago. I haven't got a screwdriver or spare fuse for the plug.

Since the sockets are fine and there's no screwdriver to open the plug safely, the most likely cause is damage inside that taped section of the cable. The tape often hides stress points where the cord bends repeatedly near the plug, causing internal wires to snap or short out. If you see damaged wires or if the vacuum works only when the cable is bent in a specific way, the mains cable needs replacing. Given your lack of tools and safety concerns with internal wiring, I would recommend taking it to a local appliance repair shop or considering a replacement unit, as fixing this safely usually requires soldering and heat-shrink tubing.
